author: taktlos
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a massive disappointment that completely loses what made the franchise iconic, and the manufactured hype around it only makes it worse. Instead of the raw, unfiltered sandbox freedom and over-the-top power fantasy of classic Vice City, Rockstar delivered a sanitized, overly restrictive experience.

You can’t even build a real criminal empire or freely buy luxury properties with your own money. Everything is locked behind scripted story progression and basic garages. On top of that, the game constantly slows you down with rigid, linear mission design, a tiny weapon wheel that forces you to run back to your car trunk for guns, punishing wanted levels, and constant relationship maintenance instead of letting you cause unrestricted chaos. Add in unstable 30 FPS performance on consoles, launch bugs, and GTA+ monetization pushed into a full-priced single-player game, and it’s clear this is a massive step backward.

The writing also feels completely watered down by modern toxic-feminist messaging. Instead of the edgy, anything-goes satire GTA used to be famous for, you are stuck babysitting a relationship meter the entire game, answering goodnight texts, holding hands, and staying strictly loyal to a flawless "girlboss" lead while classic sandbox freedom gets stripped out. Worst of all, anytime longtime fans point out how sanitized and restrictive this game actually is, defenders immediately throw around lazy buzzwords like "incel" to shut down valid criticism, even when it’s obvious the classic GTA soul is missing.

Verdict: All hype, pretty graphics, and zero GTA soul. A sluggish, preachy mess that forgets why people loved Grand Theft Auto in the first place.
